correctness.rationale: From Git RESULT.md blob 40046ba7, check the stationary anomalous covariance equation 0=-gamma B-iJ(sigma_x B+B sigma_x)+gamma diag(M1,M2): substitution B_11=mu q+d, B_22=mu q-d, B_12=-i chi q gives exact zero using mu=gamma^2/(gamma^2+4J^2), chi=2gamma J/(gamma^2+4J^2). Normal N is stationary by symmetry and damping. The quadrature covariance has local determinants u=a^2-h^2(mu^2 c^2+s^2), intermode det=-w^2 and detV=(u-w^2)^2, where w=h chi|c|. Since mu^2+chi^2=mu, u>=w^2; standard two-mode Gaussian PT invariant gives nu_tilde_minus=sqrt(u)-w. With K^2-S^2=1, 2nu=y[sqrt(1+(1-mu^2)z^2)-chi z]. R(z) strictly convex, derivative vanishes only at z*=sqrt(mu/(1-mu^2)) and R(z*)=1/sqrt(1+mu). Restrict z to [0,S] for optimal phase. The entangled phase interval roots follow exactly from quadratic R(z)<1/y; the arccos difference scales 1/S=Theta(exp(-2r)). Direct independent numerical parameter check with mu=.4, chi=sqrt(.24), y=1.2,S=2.5 and cos delta=.3 confirmed covariance determinant and PT eigenvalue within numerical precision. Limits J,gamma>0, r>=0 and y>=1 are respected.
